references.text: Describes the Gershonites' responsibility for the tabernacle's coverings and hangings, which they are to carry under the supervision of Aaron and his sons.
Moses gave carts and oxen to the Gershonites and Merarites to transport the tabernacle's equipment, under the supervision of Ithamar, Aaron's son.
Shows that Aaron's sons must first cover the holy things before the Kohathites come to carry them – a parallel example of priestly oversight over the Levites' work.
The Merarites' service was also to be under the supervision of Ithamar, Aaron's son – the same principle of priestly authority over the Levites' work.
Ithamar, Aaron's son, had oversight of the Levites' service at the tabernacle, confirming the leading role of Aaron's family.
Eleazar, Aaron's son, was high priest over the leaders of the Levites and had supervision over those who cared for the sanctuary.
The Levites' task was to serve under Aaron's sons in the house of the Lord – a continuation of the principle from the wilderness journey.
